Audit 1073's unfiltered WebSearch of the exact title returned the publisher copies frontiersin.org/journals/remote-sensing/articles/10.3389/frsen.2022.987105/full and /pdf, on which the byline (Francesco Caruso, Giacomo Giorli, Lijun Dong, Likun Zhao, Mingming Liu, Mingli Lin, Songhai Li), title, Frontiers in Remote Sensing volume 3 article 987105 (2022), Methods 2.1 and 2.2, Results 3.2 and the licence were re-read. Cuvier, 1829), Living, found in the wild, Artiodactyla (Cetacea as suborder), Phocoenidae, with China in its country list (reached from audit 1073's own search). Not a repeat of main: no main record carries 10.3389/frsen.2022.987105; N. phocaenoides IS on main under sense_echolocation from a different paper (docs/views/audit/corrected/mammal-groups.jsonl line 51, Akamatsu et al. 2005, 10.1098/rspb.2004.3024, inspection range), so the unit's 'no record for N. phocaenoides' was wrong; main also has N. asiaeorientalis (desk-d516, on-axis click parameters) and a genus-level oa-7 row.

value: centroid frequency (fc) mean 130.7 kHz (SD 3.8), n = 2,654 clicks
measurement: centroid frequency (fc) [kHz], mean +/- SD of the clicks classified as finless porpoise echolocation clicks (Results 3.2, Signal features)
method: Methods > 2.2 Acoustic data analysis: 'The signal parameters measured for each echolocation click are 1) Pulse duration (d) [µs]; 2) Peak frequency (fp) [Hz]; 3) Centroid frequency (fc) [kHz]; 4) −3 dB Bandwidth [kHz] (BW−3dB); 5) RootMean Square Bandwidth (BWRMS); 6) QRMS [kHz]; 7) Number of zero crossing (Zc) [#]; 8) Inter-click interval (ICI) [ms].' (joined from reader pieces) and 'All parameters were measured as described in Caruso et al. (2020a).' (the parameters are not defined in this paper). Clicks were found by a MATLAB routine with a 3 kHz high-pass filter and a Teager-Kaiser operator over an adaptive threshold, a window extracted around each click peak; a supervised classifier (Cubic SVM) separated finless porpoise clicks from other short broadband pulses, and 'A trained operator analyzed the waveform and spectrogram of the classified signals using the software Raven Lite (Bioacoustics Research Program, Cornell Lab of Ornithology).' (joined from reader pieces). 'Information on the position of the source was not considered, and therefore on the direction of origin and the distance of the recorded animals.' (joined from reader pieces). 'The variability of signal features is illustrated using boxplots and described as mean ± standard deviation.' Recording (2.1): each station 'equipped with a single channel SoundTrap recorder (ST300 HF, Ocean Instruments Ltd., New Zealand)'; 'A recording duty cycle of 5 min every 30 min (16.6%) was used, with a sampling frequency of 288 kHz.'
conditions: Free-ranging Indo-Pacific finless porpoises, southwestern waters of Hainan Island, China; passive acoustic monitoring from 10 stations (metal frames anchored to the ocean bottom; platform #2 lost), 25 February 2018 to 16 June 2019 (476 days). 'In total, 2,654 short pulses were identified as clicks from IPFPs within 51 files (5-min recordings) across eight PAM sites (stations #9 and #10 had no detections).' The abstract describes the same sample differently: 'measured for 2,654 short-narrowband pulses detected within 47 days across the 10 sites.' The n is clicks pooled over files and sites, not animals; the paper does not estimate the number of individuals, and animals were not seen, so species identity rests on the classifier and the operator check. DESIGN: source position was not considered (Methods sentence quoted in method), so the clicks are of unknown direction and range and no on-axis selection was made; the value is a mean over clicks of unknown aspect and should not be read alongside on-axis values (such as the on-axis N. asiaeorientalis rows of desk-d516) without that qualification. On-axis clicks from Gong et al. (2019) were used only for the detection-range model. The Methods list peak frequency in Hz while the Results print kHz. Article type printed: Brief Research Report. Same Results section: BWRMS 16.7 ± 1.5 kHz, BW−3dB 15.5 ± 3.9 kHz, QRMS 8 ± 1, zero crossings 22 ± 4, ICI 'an average of 0.02 ± 0.9 s', and 'the mean SPLpk resulted 143 ± 4 dB re 1 µPa' (received level at unknown range, not a source level); none filed.
